chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Hisham ibn Salim has been transmitted by me from my father and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Walid - may Allah be pleased with them both - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari together, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, Al-Hasan ibn Zhurayf, and Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim. I have also narrated it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr and Ali ibn Al-Hakam together, from Hisham ibn Salim Al-Jawaliqi.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them both (honorific for two people)
key_terms.عَنْ أَبِي: From my father (referring to the author's father)

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in the chain for Hisham ibn Salim's hadiths in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous verification of the *isnad* for Hisham ibn Salim, a key narrator in the Kufan school. By listing multiple independent chains—such as those through al-Hassan ibn Zafar and Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himiri—the text underscores the reliability (*tawatur*) of these reports in Shia jurisprudence. This emphasis on chain integrity reflects the early Shia scholarly commitment to preserving the Prophet's teachings through trusted companions and successors.
